limits: The local trace formulas and tail estimates do not establish global Weil positivity. The Poisson-coordination step is programmatic here, normalization is explicitly error-sensitive, and the geometric route supplies interpretation rather than a completed proof.
title: Local trace identities do not assemble without a global normalization law

claim: At the Archimedean place, simultaneous exact compact support in a variable and its Fourier dual is impossible, so the function-field-style intersection is replaced by a concentration problem. Prolate spheroidal modes diagonalize the product of the two projections and sharply order the near-intersection; scaling-compatible Fourier self-duality also feeds concrete Sonine functions into this setting. A later self-adjoint prolate extension and Dirac square root use that ordered localization to reproduce the Archimedean high-energy term in the zeta-zero counting law.
historical_or_program_relation: The program evolves from repairing a failed exact-support transplant, through an explicit self-dual Sonine construction, to a self-adjoint ultraviolet model whose target is the coarse Archimedean counting invariant.
limits: Controlled concentration is not exact common support, and matching a high-energy counting law is much weaker than reproducing individual zeros, their oscillations, or the prime terms of an explicit formula. The cited stages do not prove RH.
title: Prolate modes replace impossible exact localization by an ordered spectral approximation

claim: The naturalness requirement and the survey-level Hilbert-Polya implication combine into an operational audit: construct the space, operator, domain, and adjoint independently; prove a complete correspondence with all nontrivial zeros; only then use self-adjointness to force real spectral parameters. Theta-weighted pairings and difference-operator inverses show why this ordering matters: their chosen kernels already generate completed-zeta or Hurwitz-zeta values, while non-self-adjointness, an abstract zeta-valued replacement for a scalar product, inverse-kernel ambiguity, and missing domain control leave no independent spectral constraint.
historical_or_program_relation: The general Hilbert-Polya motivation is sharpened by later constructions that make answer-encoding diagnosable at the precise kernel, inverse, inner-product, and domain stages.
limits: Encoding zeta in a kernel or boundary condition is not by itself a refutation; such a construction could still become explanatory if its choices are independently canonical and its operator theory is completed. The cited models do not currently establish those conditions or a no-go theorem.
title: A Hilbert-Polya model must constrain zeros rather than install them

claim: Poisson-derived functional-equation reflection explains the zeta zero set's symmetric orbits, and affine label maps render a hypothetical off-line orbit as a rectangle; neither operation fixes each point on the critical line. Modified PT symmetry has the analogous limitation on an operator spectrum: it enforces paired labels or complex-conjugate eigenvalues but does not supply self-adjointness or the required reality pattern. Continuous parameter-independence could turn discreteness into fixed-point rigidity, but only if that invariance is independently proved.
historical_or_program_relation: Analytic reflection is repeatedly imported into spectral language; the later operator proposals reveal that setwise invariance must be supplemented by a genuine rigidity mechanism before it can bear the RH conclusion.
limits: The functional equation, affine-label family, and modified PT action are distinct symmetries on distinct spaces. The parameter-independence premise is RH-equivalent in the cited construction, and no source here proves it or derives spectral reality from symmetry alone.
title: Reflection symmetries organize spectral labels without forcing reality

claim: Concrete boundary models separate three levels of spectral legitimacy. A rank-two boundary trap exhibits destructive interference as an actual confinement mechanism, and half-line self-adjoint extension theory turns momentum ambiguity into cosine and sine sectors with definite gamma phases. By contrast, evaluating a formal Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunction at zero produces the desired zeta secular equation before an admissible common domain is known. The black-hole dilation program explicitly tries to close that gap by deriving a phase-space boundary identification from a finite D4 action and gauged CPT, with parity routing modes to zeta or Dirichlet-beta conditions.
historical_or_program_relation: The research burden shifts from choosing a boundary that reproduces zeros to deriving a boundary or extension from independent symmetry and domain principles that also survive time evolution.
limits: The trapping and half-line examples do not themselves realize the Riemann spectrum. The Hurwitz-zeta construction remains formal, while gauged CPT, the physical quotient, completeness, and stability of the black-hole model are assumptions or open problems rather than validated boundary selection.
title: The boundary condition is the quantization hinge, not a finishing detail

claim: For the xp dilation flow, phase-space regularization is semantically active. Lower cutoffs yield the smooth Riemann term as present, emission-like levels, while a bounding box yields a divergent continuum count minus that term and hence a missing-state or absorption reading. A symplectic cutoff comparison preserves area and the leading count across coordinates, but phase, boundary data, regulator-dependent linear terms, discreteness, and the oscillatory zero contribution are not preserved by that coarse invariant.
historical_or_program_relation: Berry-Keating and Connes-style constructions are best compared by holding the bulk dilation dynamics fixed and varying the regulated region; later exact finite-model comparisons isolate which asymptotic terms survive and which remember the cutoff.
limits: The constructions are not isospectral realizations of one established operator, and agreement of leading Weyl terms does not choose between emission and absorption. None of the cited counts supplies the missing boundary conditions or explains the individual Riemann zeros.
title: The same dilation flow supports counted-level and missing-level readings

claim: Matching the smooth zero staircase leaves the arithmetic oscillation problem untouched. One inverse construction can map a desired density fluctuation into a wiggly phase-space boundary and then into localized waves whose shapes differ with exact-zero phase data, showing concretely where fine spectral information can reside. Conversely, tested inverse-spectrum perturbations and prime-indexed level deletions produce smooth multi-scale arctangent responses and fail to reproduce the irregular zero count. The comparison makes independent generation of the boundary phase, not its post hoc reconstruction, the explanatory test.
historical_or_program_relation: After semiclassical xp counting established the coarse law, later programs split into inverse boundary encoding and attempts to generate fluctuations through modified levels; their contrast distinguishes representational capacity from a predictive spectral mechanism.
limits: The inverse boundary is constructed from the target fluctuation and is unique only in a stated monotone regime, so it risks answer-encoding. The failed perturbation and deletion experiments concern particular inverse models and do not constitute a no-go theorem for all bulk or boundary dynamics.
title: Prescribed spectral wiggles require an independent law to become explanatory

claim: The sine-kernel determinant supplies a candidate hierarchy for zeta zero statistics, while characteristic-polynomial moments isolate a universal ensemble factor only after source-specific arithmetic factors are removed. Katz-Sarnak sharpens the comparison by making the arithmetic family determine the compact symmetry type. Arithmetic quantum chaos adds an operator-level correction: when Laplace spectra violate a generic random-matrix prediction, Hecke spectra generated by the same arithmetic structure may be the observables that carry the relevant random-matrix law.
historical_or_program_relation: The analogy develops from a single-spectrum spacing conjecture, through factorized moment predictions and family-dependent symmetry, to reassignment of the statistical model from the geometric Hamiltonian to commuting arithmetic operators.
limits: The finite-field family model is the proved case cited here; number-field and zeta predictions remain asymptotic or conjectural. Ensemble agreement neither constructs a Hilbert-Polya operator nor proves RH, and finite-height zero data may converge slowly.
title: Random-matrix symmetry belongs to a family and an operator, not to arithmetic in general

claim: Bounds across number-field embeddings compress allowable traces into a lattice-like tube; after the trace-length map this compression can produce large periodic-orbit multiplicities and exceptional spectral statistics. The same arithmeticity supplies an infinite commensurator and commuting nonlocal Hecke correspondences, which preserve Laplace energy while adding labels and identities useful for individual eigenfunction questions. Thus the structure that spoils a generic chaos model can simultaneously create stronger proof probes.
historical_or_program_relation: Arithmetic quantum-chaos work moves from diagnosing excess length degeneracy to exploiting the corresponding nonlocal arithmetic symmetries, replacing a simple universal-statistics expectation by an obstruction-and-instrument account.
limits: The multiplicity asymptotics and the critical exponent discussion include compressed assumptions, and subcritical degeneracy only removes a diagonal contradiction rather than proving GOE. The Hecke mechanism is specific to arithmetic quotients and is not identified here with a zeta-zero operator.
title: Hidden arithmetic structure is both a universality obstruction and a spectral instrument

claim: Turning a phase expression into a labeled critical-line zero equation gains more than an aggregate staircase only if existence, branch choice, monotonicity, and uniqueness are established independently for every label. The proposed saturation argument compares the resulting critical-line count with the whole-strip count, while a separate branch audit shows that the integer correction to a principal argument can already contain the global staircase N(T) and then cancel the apparent arithmetic phase. This makes dependency tracing essential: count equality cannot validate the premise if the same count entered the phase convention or monotonicity claim.
historical_or_program_relation: Computational phase formulas sharpen the localization of known zeros, but later auditing relocates the proof burden from numerical root finding to global uniqueness and branch bookkeeping independent of the target count.
limits: This does not invalidate phase-based numerical localization or prove that every phase equation is circular. It applies to the cited dependency chain and branch convention; the authors themselves disclaim a rigorous saturation proof.
title: Phase conventions can import the zero count a spectral equation claims to recover

claim: The Hilbert-Polya target requires a natural operator with a discrete, complete spectral correspondence, but two Lie-Noether quantizations reduce their symmetry-preserving PDEs only to fixed temporal modes multiplied by arbitrary functions of a scaling coordinate. The reductions therefore show exactly what the selected classical symmetries determine and what they leave continuous. This aligns with the separate domain audit: discreteness cannot be inferred from a formal Hamiltonian or symmetry algebra without boundary conditions, admissible state space, adjoint, and completeness.
historical_or_program_relation: Later variational and formal-operator proposals make the old Hilbert-Polya requirement more precise by exhibiting residual functional freedom that only additional global or domain data could remove.
limits: The conclusion concerns the displayed symmetry prescriptions, not all quantizations of the classical Hamiltonian; extra boundary data could discretize the remaining amplitudes. It is a diagnosis of an unmet step, not a proof that no self-adjoint realization exists.
title: Symmetry-preserving quantization can leave a continuum of unconstrained modes

claim: Classical completion first removes gamma and pole artifacts so the nontrivial divisor is an entire, reflection-symmetric zero problem; pairing zeros under that functional-equation involution and passing to a quadratic invariant then removes the duplicated orientation and lowers the order of the secondary zero sequence. The second representation is therefore a quotient of symmetry made visible by the first, not an independent relabeling of raw zeta zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: The 1953 completion-and-confinement treatment supplies the symmetry data that the 2003 secondary-zeta program later uses as a representation-reduction device.
limits: Neither step proves that zeros lie on the critical line or even supplies a zero-existence theorem in the cited units. The quadratic reduction depends on the functional symmetry, and its exact transformed product is not certified from the OCR-damaged span.
title: Completion exposes the zero involution; a quadratic coordinate then quotients it

claim: In the explicit formula, a zero with real part beta contributes on the x^beta scale, so zero exclusion controls prime-counting error; after smoothing, a single low conjugate zero pair can instead certify oscillation once the remaining zero tail is bounded. Error bounds and Omega results are thus two directions of the same zero-to-prime transform: globally constrain the divisor to bound arithmetic error, or isolate part of the divisor to force arithmetic fluctuation.
historical_or_program_relation: Hardy's 1916 smoothed oscillation mechanism and later completed-zeta/explicit-formula presentations expose complementary uses of the zero sum that the 2003 survey places on the PNT-to-RH scale.
limits: The zero sum requires its prescribed symmetric or smoothed interpretation, and the smoothed error is not interchangeable with the raw summatory error. The relation supplies no RH proof and no automatic transfer of a smoothed Omega bound to a sharp unsmoothed one.
title: The explicit formula transfers zero geometry into both prime-counting error and oscillation

claim: Hardy's phase normalization turns critical-line zeros into sign geometry of a real function, so rigorously signed changes provide a lower bound on line zeros. A separate argument-principle or global counting total closes the logical gap: equality between the line lower bound and the total zero count leaves no room for off-line zeros in the bounded region.
historical_or_program_relation: The historical Gram-point representation became a scalable computational search coordinate, while Backlund/Turing-style global counts remained the completeness certificate rather than being replaced by the sign search.
limits: Sign changes alone can miss even-multiplicity zeros and do not certify the global total. The conclusion is bounded by the verified height and depends on rigorous evaluation and counting errors; it does not extrapolate to RH.
title: Critical-line sign changes become finite RH certification only after an independent total count

claim: A fast approximation becomes a rigorous routing device only when paired with an absolute-error envelope: signs whose magnitudes clear the margin are accepted, while small or shifted cases receive finer sampling or longer direct evaluation. Later runs separated truncation, interpolation, and arithmetic errors and used zero-count identities plus adversarial Gram-block patterns to audit whether the adaptive search could miss exceptions.
historical_or_program_relation: Lehmer's selective SWAC recomputation develops into shifted-point stabilization and method-specific error certification at much larger heights, with conservation identities and counterfactual block patterns added as explicit checks on the search policy.
limits: Shifted evaluations change the measurement protocol and must not be pooled silently with unshifted statistics. Related programs and hardware reruns are not fully independent implementations, and adjacent-block recovery, though successful on observed cases, is not logically complete.
title: Certified uncertainty drives adaptive zero computation and audits its own heuristics

claim: The Riemann-von Mangoldt count supplies a changing local density whose reciprocal is the natural gap unit; unfolding by that density removes deterministic thinning and turns zero clusters into translation-invariant, unit-density observables. Matching matrix size to the same mean spacing then allows finite-height zeta gaps, n-level correlations, and finite-N characteristic-polynomial statistics to be compared in one calibrated coordinate.
historical_or_program_relation: The progression runs from normalized gap statistics to determinantal n-level tests and finite-size random-matrix corrections, while the Hilbert-Polya program treats the residual unfolded fluctuations as constraints on any natural spectral object.
limits: Unfolding removes the mean scale but does not establish GUE statistics, construct an operator, or prove RH. Finite-N agreement and local correlation laws do not by themselves determine global arithmetic information or extreme gaps.
title: Unfolding is the common calibration that makes zero statistics comparable to random matrices

claim: Mean-count or spacing agreement is only the first constraint on a Hilbert-Polya candidate. To turn spectral reality into RH, the construction must define a legitimate self-adjoint domain, prove that every nontrivial zero and no spurious state enters the correspondence, and reproduce the coupled arithmetic, analytic, and dynamical consequences encoded by explicit or trace formulas without defining the space from the zeros themselves.
historical_or_program_relation: Survey and trace-formula diagnostics sharpen the inverse spectral program into a coupled specification; the later difference-operator Hamiltonian illustrates why formal eigenfunctions and a boundary secular equation still fail until the common domain, adjoint, and completeness problems are solved.
limits: These units provide falsifiers and proof obligations, not a no-go theorem or a constructed operator. Self-adjointness would imply spectral reality only after the exhaustive zero-state correspondence is independently established.
title: A spectral match needs a domain, a complete zero correspondence, and arithmetic trace data

claim: Locally, factoring out a close zero pair makes the logarithmic derivative an explicit pair field plus an analytic background, so the nearby critical point is an analytic pushforward of the unfolded gap. Globally, Littlewood boundary integrals compress derivative-zero locations into horizontal-displacement moments. The two observables therefore measure the same derived zero geometry at different resolutions: a microscopic gap-to-critical-point map and a macroscopic displacement mass.
historical_or_program_relation: Classical aggregate derivative-zero counts and moments are complemented by the CUE-guided close-pair expansion, while later unconditional inequalities compare left derivative displacement with right zeta-zero displacement without locating individual roots.
limits: The local random-matrix correspondence and conditioned background average do not prove the global displacement inequalities. Aggregate moments do not recover nearest-neighbor configurations, and the hypotheses and normalizations of the local and global results differ.
title: Derivative zeros compress zero geometry at microscopic and aggregate scales

claim: Differentiating the functional equation converts left-side derivative zeros into zeros of a reflected gamma-factor or auxiliary function. Boundary domination can transfer a zero count by Rouche, while quotienting the auxiliary function by zeta and applying Littlewood converts the mismatch into a boundary log-modulus integral; telescoping higher logarithmic derivatives extends this boundary-size strategy to kth derivatives.
historical_or_program_relation: The first-derivative far-left comparison by Rouche develops into quotient-based horizontal-displacement estimates and then a higher-derivative reflection-Littlewood-telescoping pipeline.
limits: Rouche zero counts and Littlewood displacement moments are different outputs and cannot be substituted for one another. The results have different regions and hypotheses, inherit gamma-factor and local pole estimates, and remain aggregate rather than pointwise statements.
title: Functional-equation reflection turns derivative-zero location into boundary size

claim: The recurring pipeline is typed: replace a hard zero set by zeros of an auxiliary differential combination, enlarge or compare that count through Littlewood or Jensen, and bound it by a shifted mollified mean square. Once arithmetic analysis supplies an explicit quadratic constant, polynomial profiles and differential coefficients become constrained control variables; Euler-Lagrange or numerical optimization then improves proportions of critical-line, derivative, or distinct zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: Conrey's two-fifths argument establishes the variational mollifier interface; later multi-piece mollifiers and xi-plus-derivative or high-derivative auxiliaries reuse it for stronger and differently typed zero statistics.
limits: A mollified mean square alone proves no zero proportion, and multiplicity conventions differ across the reductions. Continuous optimizers may only describe an infimum until approximated by admissible polynomials, imported mean-value theorems carry length restrictions, and displayed numerical witnesses do not prove global optimality.
title: Mollified mean squares turn zero counts into constrained variational objectives

claim: A holomorphic two-shift moment family is a generating representation: differential operators are applied in the shift variables only after a uniform undifferentiated estimate is available, and Cauchy contours control extraction of the desired zeta derivatives. In the multi-piece setting, divided-difference poles must first be converted to integral forms and dual contributions recombined so specialization at coincident shifts remains regular.
historical_or_program_relation: The two-shift local mean used in the two-fifths proof becomes a reusable lifting device in later multi-piece mollifier moments, where explicit pole cancellation is part of the interface rather than informal algebra.
limits: Uniformity on the small-shift contours is essential; the method does not license formal differentiation of an O-term. Apparent-pole cancellation can require the full symmetric sum, so isolated pieces need not have a regular coincident-shift limit.
title: Small shifts generate differentiated moments without differentiating an uncontrolled error

claim: A truncated Mobius inverse is useful through two distinct obligations: convolution creates an exact initial range where coefficients of LM-1 vanish, while mean-square, large-sieve, or contour estimates suppress the remaining nonsquare and tail coefficients only in aggregate. This algebraic-gap plus analytic-residual decomposition explains why the same finite inverse can support family zero questions and typical short-interval zeta comparisons.
historical_or_program_relation: Barban-Vehov interpolation makes the exact low-range gap explicit in Dirichlet-L zero work; quadratic-family and short-interval programs retain that cancellation core but redesign support, smoothing, and norm estimates for their averaging geometry.
limits: The exact cancellation ranges and some endpoints are OCR-sensitive, and the family constructions are not identical. L2 closeness is not pointwise inversion or uniform short-interval control, and nonsquare contributions are analytically bounded rather than annihilated.
title: Effective mollifiers combine exact coefficient gaps with averaged analytic suppression

claim: A local zero creates a reciprocal-distance signal in zeta'/zeta, while Euler-product positivity bounds a nonnegative combination of such signals at several heights. Choosing a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial determines that combination and compresses admissible zero-free inequalities into a scalar objective; spectral-factor autocorrelations later make nonnegativity automatic during numerical search.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical three-height positivity mechanism develops into degree-indexed polynomial optimization and then a factorized, constraint-preserving search embedded in a mollified detector with separately auditable interior, exterior, and zero-tail errors.
limits: The polynomial is only one component of the zero-free proof: local analytic growth, remote-zero tails, verified finite ranges, and numerical error bounds remain load-bearing. A surrogate-optimal polynomial need not optimize the final finite region, and the searches do not certify a global optimum.
title: Arithmetic positivity and nonnegative trigonometric polynomials turn a putative zero into a scalar contradiction

claim: A rigorously complete low-zero census can replace a generic zero-count remainder by subtracting the enumerated zeros from a global reciprocal-square sum, while a uniform counting theorem controls the remote tail. In a continuation-style zero-free proof, finite-height certificates then provide the lower-stage rectangle needed to license the next analytic detector, so computational evidence functions as a bounded lemma rather than inductive evidence for RH.
historical_or_program_relation: Large Turing-style verified runs supply certified finite data that later explicit-region work consumes in tail bounds and proposes to compose through an envelope of overlapping finite regions.
limits: The transfer is valid only with completeness, precision, provenance, and the stated test-function/counting hypotheses. It neither extrapolates RH beyond the cutoff nor closes the proposed high-altitude envelope gaps unless each tiny finite exclusion is independently certified.
title: Finite zero certification becomes a quantitative input to global zero-free inequalities

claim: Contour proofs of the prime number theorem consume a zero-free boundary as a height-dependent allowable shift; optimizing contour height balances the decay gained by moving left against truncation and zeta-log-derivative costs. Consequently, finite zero-free regions must be compared as envelopes over the actual height range, because downstream PNT errors inherit the usable width function rather than a constant or asymptotic shape in isolation.
historical_or_program_relation: Vinogradov-Korobov contour optimization explains how improved exclusion propagates to primes, while modern explicit-region work treats competing formulas and finite constants as range-dependent modules for explicit PNT bounds.
limits: A wider region improves only the portion of a downstream argument that depends on width; all other finite-range ingredients and log-derivative bounds must remain valid. These regions remain far from the square-root-scale PNT error implied by RH.
title: A zero-free envelope is a modular interface from analytic exclusion to PNT decay

claim: Positive quadratic statistics of zero differences become useful when their Fourier support lies inside the band where the explicit formula evaluates them. Entire-function majorants use that band to bound interval pair counts, while a tunable pair-correlation kernel uses the same positivity to bound one linear Fourier mode through weighted local second differences. Both routes trade inaccessible phases for a measurable zero-difference energy.
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery-style band-limited pair correlation is refined in one direction by de Branges extremal approximation and in another by an energy inequality tailored to fractional-part cancellation.
limits: The two optimizations have different targets and admissible kernels; an optimal interval majorant need not optimize the one-frequency bound. Conclusions remain conditional on the available Fourier band or additional pair-correlation uniformity, and the diagonal must be separated so multiplicity is not read as a close distinct pair.
title: Band-limited pair statistics can control counts or a single zero Fourier mode

claim: The explicit formula makes primes and zeros dual descriptions: the leading zero-ordinate distribution can become uniform after normalization while Fourier modes resonant with log prime powers survive as a lower-order periodic bias. Replacing zeta's von Mangoldt weights by the corresponding Selberg-class coefficients preserves the resonance selection rule, showing that the bias comes from Euler-product frequency support rather than zeta notation.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical prime-zero reconstruction is sharpened into a lower-order distribution theorem for fractional zero ordinates and then transported to primitive Selberg-class L-functions.
limits: A lower-order bias does not contradict leading equidistribution and is not a statement about consecutive gaps or GUE statistics. The generalized result changes the admissible test class and arithmetic weights, and it does not assert that every frequency survives.
title: Prime-power frequencies survive beneath leading equidistribution as a periodic zero bias

claim: Unfolding an automorphic average turns the constant or scalar projection into a Mellin-Eisenstein object whose contour residues at nontrivial zeta zeros appear as convergence exponents or crossing terms. But an admissible theta series can be orthogonal to every such residue, so the existence of zeta poles in the ambient spectral decomposition does not ensure that a chosen observable detects them; projection design controls zero observability.
historical_or_program_relation: The modular-stability program reads zeta zeros as horocycle error exponents and demonstrates an annihilating test function, while the scalar modular-bootstrap program deliberately projects to a zero-bearing channel and studies how regularization retains the residue mechanism.
limits: The bridges require the stated modular invariance, smoothness, decay, continuation, and regularization hypotheses. Vanishing coefficients for one observable neither remove the ambient zeros nor refute the representation, and numerical bootstrap cancellation is not a proved zero identity or evidence for RH.
title: Automorphic projection can expose zeta-zero residues—or annihilate them

claim: After truncating a zero-driven sine series, simultaneous approximation aligns finitely many phases and recurrence transfers the resulting transform growth to distant arithmetic oscillation. The competing finite-range bias can nevertheless persist extraordinarily long because the eventual winning term grows through iterated logarithms, so a rigorous asymptotic sign reversal and an apparently stable computational sign are compatible.
historical_or_program_relation: Hardy's phase-alignment argument supplies a mechanism behind the eventual reversal of the prime-counting bias, while computational history reframes its iterated-log scale as an epistemic obstruction to numerical extrapolation.
limits: The argument does not locate the first reversal, show that one sign is typical at all large scales, or convert recurrence into RH evidence. The finite/tail split and zero-counting input remain essential to the oscillation proof.
title: Finite phase alignment can prove eventual oscillation while explaining its computational invisibility

claim: Averaging log|f| along almost-periodic vertical translates produces a convex Jensen function whose slope differences give stripwise zero frequency; integrating boundary log modulus in Littlewood's lemma instead yields zero counts or first moments of horizontal displacement. Both mechanisms compress a planar divisor through its logarithmic potential, but they retain different coordinates: vertical frequency across strip boundaries versus weighted distance from a reference line.
historical_or_program_relation: Jessen-Tornehave mean motion provides a value-distribution route to strip frequencies, while Levinson-Conrey and derivative-zero arguments use Littlewood boundary integrals as a zero-counting and displacement interface.
limits: The almost-periodic Jensen theorem needs its mean-convergence and differentiability conditions, whereas the zeta applications require contour, normalization, and boundary estimates. Equality of the two compressed observables is not claimed, and neither projection recovers individual zeros.
title: Log-modulus potentials encode vertical zero frequency and horizontal displacement through different projections

claim: Scaling ordinates by conductor produces unit-density family statistics, while splitting by functional-equation sign exposes distinct orthogonal symmetry kernels. A nonnegative band-limited one-level test then converts the limiting density into central nonvanishing bounds, and the parity-sensitive off-diagonal prime-Kloosterman term explains where SO(even) and SO(odd) separate even though their diagonal contributions agree.
historical_or_program_relation: The general n-level random-matrix comparison is specialized into a one-level arithmetic instrument: conductor and parity choose the symmetry class, Fourier support determines what the trace formula can see, and extremal positivity turns that information into population bounds.
limits: These are family-average results with restricted Fourier support, not statements that each L-function satisfies RH or is nonvanishing. Symmetry identification depends on the arithmetic off-diagonal analysis, and a broader test support requires new cancellation estimates rather than formal random-matrix analogy.
title: Family symmetry becomes arithmetic only when scaled zero density is paired with positive tests
